As far as the recent surge, health experts are pointing to exposure events in Sugarcreek and Bloomfield. [...] The Ashtabula County Health Department first reported two cases of measles back on July 23.

People who have weakened immune systems may take longer to experience symptoms.

According to experts, anyone seeking testing should contact their healthcare provider. You should not arrive at a healthcare facility without calling ahead if measles is suspected.

title: One Vaccine, Three Supply Chains: The Hidden ...
snippet:
A measles outbreak, for example, could sharply increase demand for a stand-alone measles vaccine while demand for rubella remained relatively stable. Manufacturers would need antigen-specific forecasts and safety stocks. Distributors would need separate replenishment algorithms. Public-health agencies could require disease-specific inventory strategies. [...] Advertisement

The debate over separating the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine is being framed largely around vaccine policy, parental choice, and public health. But the pharmaceutical industry should be asking a different question: What happens to the supply chain when one established combination vaccine becomes three separate products? [...] At one physician practice the incremental burden may look modest. Across millions of vaccination encounters, small operational changes become material system-level requirements.

## Demand Forecasting Becomes Disease-Specific

Combination vaccines naturally aggregate demand: demand for measles, mumps, and rubella protection moves through the system as one forecast. Separation breaks that relationship.
